subject: astronomy
title: Main Sequence, Giants and White Dwarfs
welcome_lead: Three populations dominate the HR diagram.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: main sequence, giants, supergiants and white dwarfs.
final_note: Each band corresponds to a stage of stellar evolution.

concepts.def: Band of hydrogen-burning stars from upper left to lower right.
Extremely luminous evolved star — Betelgeuse, Rigel.
Hot, faint remnant in the lower-left of the HR diagram.
Region where stars pulsate, including Cepheids.
Group of stars with similar age and composition.

walkthroughs.body_html: The main sequence runs diagonally from hot-bright (upper left) to cool-faint (lower right). Mass determines position: a 10 solar mass O star sits top-left; a 0.1 solar mass M dwarf sits bottom-right.
Red giants sit upper right. Supergiants sit further up. Betelgeuse is a red supergiant; Rigel is a blue supergiant. Both are massive and short-lived.
The white dwarf region lies lower left — hot but tiny, hence faint. They cool slowly over billions of years, fading along a cooling track that runs to lower right.
